FeatureId.description: A feature's ID: 8 characters of Crockford's base32 in lower case (digits and letters but i, l, o, and u).

LogLevel.description: An event's level, from the most severe: error, warn, info, debug, trace.

request.description:
`read_logs`' request: the session's recent log events, of a level and every level more
severe, of one feature or all, after a cursor.

after.description:
Read the events after this one: the last read's `next`; or null, from the oldest
kept. Refused if it's past the session's newest event.

feature.description:
The feature whose events to read (an event's feature, or its spans'), or null for
every event.

level.description:
The least severe level to read: it and every level more severe (`info` reads error,
warn, and info).

limit.description: How many events to read at most.

session.description: The session's ID, as `open` gave it.

request.title: ReadLogsRequest

FeatureId.description: A feature's ID: 8 characters of Crockford's base32 in lower case (digits and letters but i, l, o, and u).

LogEvent.description:
One event a session kept. Its time and its place among events of other threads depend
on the machine and on scheduling: diagnostics, never results.

at_ms.description: When it happened, in milliseconds since the session opened.

feature.description: The feature it's of, its own or its innermost span's: null for an event of none.

message.description: Its message, then its other fields (`key=value`); cut, ending in `…`, to fit one read.

seq.description: Its number in the session, from 1, one more for each event the session kept.

spans.description:
The spans it happened in, from the command's down: the command (with `model=published`
for a read of the published model), then each span within it, its name and fields:
`rebuild revision=2 fresh=false`, a rebuild step's `recompute_step feature=f0000001
key=… job=make`, a kernel request's `worker_call … op=Fillet`, and a worker's own
lines' `worker_lines trace=…`.

LogLevel.description: An event's level, from the most severe: error, warn, info, debug, trace.

dropped.description:
How many events the session's buffer dropped since it opened, oldest first, to keep
within its bound.

next.description:
Where the next read goes on from, its `after`: the last event returned, if the read
stopped at its limit or at 1 MiB of text; else the session's newest event.
